title: Mosaic handoff controller: latency-driven pinning + capacity-aware failover
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem: production traffic occasionally experiences cross-region spikes where a small fraction of requests see large latency regressions (>3x p95) when one region is saturated. We need a regional routing controller that balances three goals: preserve low-latency locality for most traffic (geo-pinning), gracefully shift load when capacity or SLOs degrade (capacity-aware steering), and keep fallbacks and hedging tight enough to avoid amplification.

Scope: build a 'Mosaic Handoff Controller' service plus routing policy primitives that: (1) compute per-region scores from latency telemetry + current capacity utilization + recent error rates; (2) enforce soft pinning policy with age-based stickiness and TTLs; (3) drive a tiered failover order with circuit-breaker integration and token-aware shedding thresholds; (4) expose config knobs in Console and safe rollout via canary and feature-flag.

Non-goals: not implementing new autoscaler behaviors (this will consume autoscaler signals) and not changing token billing logic in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller produces a per-request routing decision record (region, variant, decision_reason) and writes it to tracing for 100% of routed requests behind the new policy. 2) Synthetic canary traffic shows p95 tail reduction >=10% for pinned requests during regional contention scenarios vs current baseline. 3) When a region's circuit-breaker trips, traffic is automatically redistributed following tiered fallback within 30s and no more than 5% traffic loss. 4) A/B rollout at 1/5/25/100% via Console flags with rollback within 5 minutes is possible. 5) New monitoring dashboards surface: region_score distribution, pin_stickiness median, shed_rate, and failover_latency. 6) Unit + integration tests cover scoring logic, TTL behavior, and circuit-breaker handoff paths.
engineering_notes:
Scoring: compute three normalized signals: latency_score (based on p50/p95/p99 buckets), capacity_score (available VCPU/GPU token slots ratio) and error_penalty (recent 1m error rate). Final region_score = weighted_sum(latency_score*0.5, capacity_score*0.35, (1-error_penalty)*0.15) with weights tunable via Console.

Pinning: requests are sticky to a region for a TTL window default 30m with exponential decay for multi-request sessions. Geo distance penalty applied for non-pinned requests when a closer region has capacity constraints.

Failover: implement soft-failover tiers (local-edge -> nearby-region -> hemispheric -> global) with circuit-breaker integration. When region utilization > 85% or p99 > configured SLO, mark as degraded and start tiered redistribution.

Load-shedding: token-aware shedding at per-customer scope when queue depth + estimated token bursts exceed capacity-to-SLO threshold; shedding is proportional and favoring non-critical routes.

Trade-offs: heavier scoring includes more telemetry and increases decision latency; we cap scoring to sampled requests (1-5%) for audit traces but use aggregated signals for per-request fast-path.

Implementation Plan: new stateless controller + in-memory LRU for session pins. Use existing steering API extension from ENG-41329.

Open questions: exact weight tuning for region_score and TTL defaults for high-variance workloads.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: internal sim & bench (2 weeks) - run controller in dry-run mode writing decisions to trace and simulation job against last 48h traffic. Phase 2: canary (1%) for non-critical routes for 48h. Phase 3: expand to 5%/25% with close ops monitoring and manual hold if shed_rate > 2x baseline. Phase 4: full rollout + postmortem. Each phase gated by runbook checks and automated SLO regression detection.

Rollback: feature flag off + immediate reversion to existing steering path. Telemetry retention for 7 days during rollout.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: region_score_heatmap, pin_ttl_distribution, hedging_latency_over_time, shed_rate_by_customer. Alerts: SLO_regression (p99 latency increase > 10% over baseline 15min), Unexpected_failover_rate (>0.5% of requests per minute), Circuit_breaker_frequent_trips (>3 trips in 5 min), Shed_spike (>3x normal). Create an oncall playbook: steps to revert flag, flush pins, and temporarily adjust backoff multipliers.
